raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Purpose On DeepSeek-V4.1 **index-source layers** (layers with their own indexer; 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36 in V4.1-Flash), the ROCm mono decode K2 builds each token's key table and key count (`KT` / `KLEN`) itself, in the same launch, because vLLM's indexer runs between K1 and K2. - `stage_split` waits for that table (`await_flags(krdy)`) and reads it with device-scope loads. - `stage_combine` does neither: it reads `KLEN[t]` with a plain load as its first step (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono/attention/back.py:521` on main). The CTAs that run combine have no split work, so they issue that load at the start of the launch, before the table-building CTAs have stored it. They read **the count the previous layer left in the shared buffer** and merge that many key chunks. On MI355X the per-XCD L2 can also serve a stale line, so the wait alone is not enough; the load needs device scope too, exactly as in `stage_split`. Where the stale count is smaller, keys are silently dropped (V4.1-Flash, TP4, 128-key chunks): - **layer 2** (after the window-only layer 1), at every position from 85 on. Past 1023 tokens it merges 1 of 5 chunks: 128 of the 512 top-k compressed keys are kept, and the other 384 plus the whole 128-key window (including the token itself) are dropped. - **layer 20** (ratio 1 after ratio 2), at most positions in 64-768. At p = 600 it merges 4 of 5 chunks and drops the whole window. Everywhere else the stale count happens to equal the right one. **Fix:** give `stage_combine` the same wait and device-scope load as `stage_split`. Layers whose table K1 builds are unchanged. ## Test Plan 1. **New regression test** `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_index_source.py` (CDNA4; TP2 / TP4; M = 1 / 6 decode rows; ratio-2 and ratio-1 sources). An index source is run after a window-only layer, and with a window-only layer's counts planted in `KLEN`. Its outputs must match, bit for bit, the same layer using K1's key table. It is deterministic. 2. **Standalone reproducer** on the image's own package (no other changes): 200 trials per case on each of 4 ranks. 3. **Stock server**, InferenceX DSv4.1 MI355X recipe with `--monokernel`, TP4, `--max-num-seqs 1`, with a debug-only check that runs every K2 twice on identical inputs. 4. **Accuracy:** forced-trajectory top-20 logprobs against vLLM *without* `--monokernel` as the reference, compared to that reference's own run-to-run floor. Benchmarks: GSM8K (InferenceX CI path), RULER CWE at 32k-128k, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval+. ## Test Result All results on MI355X (gfx950) with the `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-e68efc68` package, which has the identical code. "Fixed" means only `back.py` patched. **Regression test** (`pytest --noconftest` in the image): before, 2 failed (`AssertionError: rank 0, ratio 2, 1 rows, trial 0: the index source's x differs from the layer's with K1's key table`); after, 2 passed (188 s). **Standalone reproducer** (outputs mismatching the reference, 800 trials per cell): | previous layer → index source | key counts (prev / own) | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | L1 → L2, ctx 3000 | 128 / 640 | 800/800 | 0/800 | | L19 → L20, ctx 600 | 428 / 640 | 800/800 | 0/800 | | L7 → L8, L13 → L14, L19 → L20 at ctx 3000, L23 → L24 ... L36 | equal | 0/800 | 0/800 | | any source with a stale count planted | — | 800/800 | 0/800 | M = 1 gives the same as M = 6. **Stock server, before the fix:** - index ratio-2 K2 calls: 3330 / 10344 mismatched (32%, which is layer 2 every time); - index ratio-1: 1148 / 17240 (6.7%, layer 20 at short positions); - every non-index layer kind: 0. The after-fix counts and a TPOT A/B will follow in a comment. **Accuracy (c1, 13 prompts at 8k-200k):** excess KL over the no-mono reference's floor, 95% CI over prompts. | config | excess KL | top-1 agreement change | |---|---|---| | `--monokernel` as is (2 servers) | +0.0040 [+0.0025, +0.0056] and +0.0026 [+0.0014, +0.0040] | -0.0055 and -0.0027 | | `--monokernel` + this fix (2 servers) | -0.0005 [-0.0014, +0.0001] and -0.0006 [-0.0013, -0.0001] | -0.0006 and -0.0002 | The fix moves the mono decode distribution onto the non-mono reference. Benchmark scores show no measurable change either way: GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval+, and RULER CWE at 128k are all within noise, about ±3-4 points at 128k. At higher concurrency, stock only uses the mono decode for ≤ 48 rows, so the bug affects low-concurrency decode. **Not run:** - the existing `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` / `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` on main. They never exercise an index source after a smaller-count layer within tolerance (numerics has no `select`; layers compares with 3-8% tolerance), so we expect no change. - a wait-only variant (without the device-scope load). - gfx942, which shares `stage_combine`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? nodes.body:
Follow-up results (MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-e68efc68` package, InferenceX DSv4.1 recipe with `--monokernel`, TP4, `--max-num-seqs 1`). "Fix" means only `back.py` patched.

**Stock server, debug check that runs every K2 twice on identical inputs (all 4 ranks agree):**

| layer kind | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| index source, ratio 2 | 3330 / 10344 mismatched (layer 2 every time) | **0** |
| index source, ratio 1 | 1148 / 17240 mismatched (layer 20 at short positions) | **0** |
| all non-index kinds | 0 | 0 |

**Performance:** smoke TPOT, 2 interleaved reps, 18 runs per arm.
- Before: median 1.559 ms, mean 1.552 ms.
- After: median 1.562 ms (+0.2%), mean 1.564 ms (+0.8%).

The difference is inside the run-to-run spread (1.51-1.60 ms). After the fix, layers 2 and 20 merge all their key chunks again, so a little extra work on those two layers is the intended behaviour.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,195 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode kernels on an index source: a layer with an
+indexer of its own, where vLLM's indexer runs between the two launches and K2
+builds the tokens' key table and key counts in the same launch that reads them.
+
+One ``DSV41MonoLayer`` serves every layer, so the key-count buffer holds the
+previous layer's counts when an index source's K2 starts. Every stage of that
+K2 must read the counts this launch builds: the layer's outputs, after a
+window-only layer (fewer keys) or with a window-only layer's counts planted in
+the buffer, must be bit for bit those of the same layer with the key table K1
+built (the layer as a non-index source).
+
+Random weights and caches in the loaded formats, one request of M decode
+tokens at a context past the top-k's 512 compressed entries, CDNA4."""
+
+import os
+import socket
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+HIDDEN, HC, WINDOW, TOPK, BLOCK, EXPERTS = 5120, 4, 128, 512, 128, 384
+CTX = 3000  # a request's first decode position
+
+
+def _on_cdna4() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version
+
+    return get_cdna_version() == 4
+
+
+def _fp8(g, *shape):
+    return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g)).clamp(-200, 200).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def _e8m0(g, *shape, lo=120, hi=126):
+    return torch.randint(lo, hi, shape, generator=g, dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+
+def _weights(tp, ratio, dev, seed):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.attention.plan import Dims
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner import AttnWeights, MonoLayerWeights
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.stages.dims import Dims as MoeDims
+
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    d, md = Dims(tp), MoeDims(tp)
+    bf = torch.bfloat16
+
+    def t(x):
+        return x.to(dev).contiguous()
+
+    def fp4(*shape):
+        u8 = torch.randint(0, 256, shape, generator=g, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        return t(u8.view(torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2))
+
+    attn = AttnWeights(
+        layer_id=seed,
+        wqkv=t(_fp8(g, 1792, HIDDEN)),
+        wqkv_scale=t(_e8m0(g, 56, HIDDEN // 32)),
+        q_norm=t((torch.rand(1280, generator=g) + 0.5).to(bf)),
+        kv_norm=t((torch.rand(512, generator=g) + 0.5).to(bf)),
+        wq_b=t(_fp8(g, d.heads * 512, 1280)),
+        wq_b_scale=t(_e8m0(g, d.heads * 16, 40)),
+        wo_a=t(_fp8(g, d.groups * 1024, d.group_k)),
+        wo_a_scale=t(_e8m0(g, d.groups * 32, d.group_k // 32)),
+        wo_b=t(_fp8(g, HIDDEN, d.groups * 1024)),
+        wo_b_scale=t(_e8m0(g, HIDDEN // 32, d.groups * 32)),
+        attn_sink=t(torch.randn(64, generator=g)),
+        cos_sin=t(torch.randn(CTX + 64, 64, generator=g).clamp(-1, 1)),
+        ratio=ratio,
+    )
+    w = MonoLayerWeights(
+        attn=attn,
+        hc_attn_fn=t(torch.randn(24, HC * HIDDEN, generator=g) * 0.02),
+        hc_attn_scale=t(torch.rand(3, generator=g) + 0.5),
+        hc_attn_base=t(torch.randn(24, generator=g) * 0.1),
+        attn_norm=t((torch.rand(HIDDEN, generator=g) + 0.5).to(bf)),
+        hc_ffn_fn=t(torch.randn(24, HC * HIDDEN, generator=g) * 0.02),
+        hc_ffn_scale=t(torch.rand(3, generator=g) + 0.5),
+        hc_ffn_base=t(torch.randn(24, generator=g) * 0.1),
+        ffn_norm=t((torch.rand(HIDDEN, generator=g) + 0.5).to(bf)),
+        gate_w=t((torch.randn(EXPERTS, HIDDEN, generator=g) * 0.02).to(bf)),
+        bias=t(torch.randn(EXPERTS, generator=g) * 0.05),
+        w13=fp4(EXPERTS, 2 * md.inter, HIDDEN // 2),
+        w13_s=t(_e8m0(g, EXPERTS * 2 * md.inter, HIDDEN // 32, lo=118, hi=122)),
+        w2=fp4(EXPERTS, HIDDEN, md.inter // 2),
+        w2_s=t(_e8m0(g, EXPERTS * HIDDEN, md.down_scale_cols, lo=118, hi=122)),
+        sgu=t(_fp8(g, 2 * md.sh_inter, HIDDEN)),
+        sgu_s=t(_e8m0(g, 2 * md.sh_inter // 32, HIDDEN // 32, lo=118, hi=122)),
+        sw2=t(_fp8(g, HIDDEN, md.sh_inter)),
+        sw2_s=t(_e8m0(g, HIDDEN // 32, md.sh_inter // 32, lo=118, hi=122)),
+    )
+    w.check(tp, EXPERTS)
+    attn.check(d)
+    return w
+
+
+def _step(M, ratio, dev, seed):
+    """A decode step of one request's M tokens from position CTX: the window
+    rows, fp8_ds_mla records and, for ratio > 0, a compressed cache and the
+    top-k vLLM's indexer would leave (min((p + 1) / ratio, 512) entries)."""
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    nblocks = 64
+    data = (torch.randn(nblocks, BLOCK, 576, generator=g) * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    data = data.view(torch.uint8)
+    rope = (torch.randn(nblocks, BLOCK, 64, generator=g) * 0.5).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    data[:, :, 448:] = rope.view(torch.uint8).reshape(nblocks, BLOCK, 128)
+    scales = torch.full((nblocks, BLOCK * 8), 120, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    rec = torch.cat([data.reshape(nblocks, -1), scales], 1).view(nblocks, BLOCK, 584)
+    pos = torch.arange(CTX, CTX + M, dtype=torch.int64)
+    ring = 16 * BLOCK
+    swa_idx = torch.full((M, 1, WINDOW), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    for i, p in enumerate(pos.tolist()):
+        swa_idx[i, 0] = (torch.arange(p - WINDOW + 1, p + 1) % ring).to(torch.int32)
+    s = dict(
+        x=torch.randn(M, HIDDEN, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16),
+        residual=torch.randn(M, HC, HIDDEN, generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16),
+        post_mix=torch.rand(M, HC, 1, generator=g) * 2,
+        res_mix=torch.rand(M, HC, HC, generator=g) * 0.5,
+        pre_mix=torch.rand(M, HC, generator=g) * 0.5,
+        positions=pos,
+        slot_mapping=pos % ring,
+        swa_cache=rec,
+        swa_indices=swa_idx,
+        swa_lens=torch.full((M,), WINDOW, dtype=torch.int32),
+        token_to_req=torch.zeros(M, dtype=torch.int32),
+    )
+    if ratio:
+        topk = torch.full((M, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+        for i, p in enumerate(pos.tolist()):
+            n = (p + 1) // ratio
+            topk[i, : min(n, TOPK)] = torch.randperm(n, generator=g)[:TOPK].int()
+        nb = (CTX + M) // ratio // BLOCK + 1
+        s.update(
+            topk_indices=topk,
+            comp_cache=rec.clone(),
+            comp_block_table=(torch.arange(nb, dtype=torch.int32) % nblocks)[None],
+        )
+    return {k: v.to(dev).contiguous() for k, v in s.items()}
+
+
+def _worker(rank, tp, port):
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+
+    os.environ["MASTER_ADDR"], os.environ["MASTER_PORT"] = "127.0.0.1", str(port)
+    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+    dist.init_process_group("gloo", rank=rank, world_size=tp)
+    dev = torch.device("cuda", rank)
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.amd.mono.runner import DSV41MonoLayer
+
+    runner = DSV41MonoLayer(tp=tp, rank=rank, group=dist.group.WORLD, device=dev)
+    window_only = _weights(tp, 0, dev, seed=1)
+    for ratio in (2, 1):
+        w = _weights(tp, ratio, dev, seed=2 + ratio)
+        for M in (1, 6):
+            before = _step(M, 0, dev, seed=10 + M)
+            step = _step(M, ratio, dev, seed=20 + M)
+            # the layer with K1's key table: the reference
+            want = [o.clone() for o in runner.forward(w, **step)]
+            for trial in range(4):
+                if trial % 2:
+                    # a window-only layer's counts in the buffer
+                    runner.klen[:M].fill_(WINDOW)
+                    runner.klen[M : 2 * M].zero_()
+                else:
+                    # the previous layer, window only, as in DeepSeek-V4.1's
+                    # layers 1 -> 2
+                    runner.forward(window_only, **before)
+                got = runner.forward(w, **step, select=lambda normed, qr: None)
+                for name, a, b in zip(("x", "res", "post", "comb", "pre"), got, want):
+                    assert torch.equal(a, b), (
+                        f"rank {rank}, ratio {ratio}, {M} rows, trial {trial}: "
+                        f"the index source's {name} differs from the layer's "
+                        "with K1's key table"
+                    )
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    dist.barrier()
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _on_cdna4(), reason="the mono kernels' CDNA4 build")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp", [2, 4])
+def test_index_source_reads_its_own_key_counts(tp):
+    if torch.accelerator.device_count() < tp:
+        pytest.skip(f"needs {tp} GPUs")
+    pytest.importorskip("flydsl")
+    with socket.socket() as s:
+        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        port = s.getsockname()[1]
+    torch.multiprocessing.spawn(_worker, args=(tp, port), nprocs=tp, join=True)

@@ -518,7 +518,16 @@ def stage_combine(c, unit):
     h = hg * COMB_HEADS + wave
     nchunk = c["nchunk"]
     ck = chunk_keys(d, s)
-    kv_len = ld_i32(a["klen"], t)
+    if const_expr("krdy" in c):
+        # An index source's key table and lengths are built in this launch
+        # (``krdy``), by other CTAs: wait for the token's and read its length
+        # past this CU's L2, as ``stage_split`` does. A combine CTA without
+        # split work gets here at the launch's start: a plain load returns the
+        # length the previous layer left, and the wrong chunk count drops keys.
+        await_flags(c, c["krdy"], 1, lambda u: t)
+        kv_len = ld_i32(a["klen"], t, CM_DEV)
+    else:
+        kv_len = ld_i32(a["klen"], t)
     nlive = (kv_len + ck - 1) // ck
     pos = ld_i32(a["pos"], 2 * t)
     sink = ld_f32(a["sink"], h) * fx.Float32(LOG2E)

+        # An index source's key table and lengths are built in this launch
+        # (``krdy``), by other CTAs: wait for the token's and read its length
+        # past this CU's L2, as ``stage_split`` does. A combine CTA without
+        # split work gets here at the launch's start: a plain load returns the
+        # length the previous layer left, and the wrong chunk count drops keys.
+        await_flags(c, c["krdy"], 1, lambda u: t)
